title: Vanishing conditional mutual information for an almost-surely constant variable
statement:
Let $\mu$ be a probability measure on a sample space $\Omega$ (or the zero measure), and let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be measurable random variables on $\Omega$ taking finitely many values in the countable sets $S$, $T$, $U$ respectively. If there is a constant $c \in S$ with $X = c$ holding $\mu$-almost everywhere, then the conditional mutual information of $X$ and $Y$ given $Z$ vanishes:
\[
I[X : Y \mid Z ; \mu] = 0.
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ is zero or a probability measure
X, Y, Z take finitely many values (finite range)
S, T, U are countable value spaces
X equals a constant c μ-almost everywhere
replaced: If $X =^{\mu\text{-a.e.}} c$ for some constant $c : S$, then $I[X : Y \mid Z;\mu] = 0$.
